lines.line: Sarius Guile? What are you doing here?
I'm leaving Morytania. It's not safe for me here anymore. Not now Vanescula is gone. It felt only right to come find you and tell you to leave as well.
Leave? I have no intention of leaving.
I'm sorry, but you don't have any hope against Lowerniel Drakan. You are not strong enough to stop him. The only choice you have is to leave or die.
I was hoping I'd find you here.
As I say, I was looking for you.
But why?
I'm leaving Morytania. It's not safe for me here anymore. Not now Vanescula is gone. Before I go though, there's something you need to know.
What is it?
Your friend, Safalaan. Lowerniel Drakan has him. He's keeping both him and Vanescula as his prisoners, in preparation for something.
Preparation for what?
I'm not sure exactly, but all vampyres have been ordered to attend a gathering outside Castle Drakan. Apparently he has an announcement to make regarding the future of Morytania.
The future of Morytania? That's not good. I need to get over there right away.
And do what? To stand against Drakan... It would be suicide!
Maybe, but I'm not abandoning my friend.
You remind me of my father. He always believed in the Myreque, even when all hope seemed lost... But the Myreque are gone now, and so is he.
They may be gone, but this fight isn't over. There's always still hope. You wouldn't have come here if you didn't believe that yourself.
Maybe...
So you're really going to go? To Castle Drakan?
I am, but hopefully not alone. I still have a couple of friends left here.
Then I guess this is goodbye, and good luck.
If you're leaving Morytania, do you have a safe way out?
Vanescula gave me some money to keep in case of an emergency. I'm paying some mercenaries from Misthalin to help me get out safely. I'll be fine. It's not me you should worry about.
If you're sure.
, I know this is about your friend, and I'm not blind to what Vanescula is, but... she's always been good to me. If you can help her...
I'll do what I can. Now I'd best get going. I need to go and see Ivan.
Good luck,.
This doesn't sound good... Can you wait here for a little while? I get the feeling I'm going to need to be well prepared for whatever you have to tell me. I'll be back as soon as I can.
I'll wait a short while, but don't take too long.
Hmm... Looks like Ivan isn't here.
Ah, there you are.
How are you doing?
Surviving.
Why are you here?
I have news from Darkmeyer. Apparently Drakan is preparing to make some sort of big announcement to the vampyres.
So you want us to go there?
That's the plan.
Back to where they died? Back to where we lost?
Ivan...
He killed them! It was like they were nothing! He killed them, and all I could do was watch!
We can't give up, Ivan!
And I haven't! I'm not Veliaf! I'm still here! I'm still helping! But I'm not you, ! I can't just go back there... I won't go back there...
He has Safalaan.
Safalaan...
I have a vampyre disguise. I can make you one as well. They'll never even know we were there.
It's not about that. I already have a disguise. I made my own a while ago. It's just...
Aren't you afraid?
More than afraid, but I won't give up on Safalaan.
When do we go?
As soon as you're ready.
Alright... Just give me a moment to get a few things together...
Okay... I think that's everything.
Are you ready to go to Darkmeyer?
I am, but it doesn't look like you are. You should put on your disguise before we set off. I think I saw it in that chest in the corner.
I am, but it doesn't look like you are. You should put on your disguise before we set off.
As ready as I'll ever be. What about you?
I'm ready.
Alright... To Darkmeyer then.
I need more time to prepare.
Fair enough.
How have things been here?
As bad as you'd expect. I'd rather not talk about it.
But you're doing okay?
Like I said... I'm surviving.
It has been a long time since I last stood before the vampyres of Morytania. I thought I had prepared myself for what I would see. Yet as I stand here now, I see that I was wrong.
To see what you have all become... The ways you stand... The ways you dress...
You disgust me.
You have become pathetic. Weak. None of you are worthy to be called vampyres anymore.
And who is to blame for that, Drakan? If we disgust you so, surely it is you, our leader, who is responsible?
Lord Jovkai... I see in my absence, you have grown arrogant once more. You always did take after your father...
But, I must confess, you speak the truth, for you are all indeed my failing. A failing that today, I will finally begin to set right.
You see, for a long time now, I have fought to return us to what we were always meant to be, but every time the answer came close, it slipped away.
Now though... Now the answer is finally in my grasp. Thanks to my dear sister, I finally have the means with which to bring about our salvation. I finally have the means for us to return home.
Home? Surely you don't mean Vampyrium? You would see us return to that wasteland? You would see us return to lives of misery?
I would see us return to lives of strength! I will take us back to a land where we will live as we were meant to! Not as royalty! Not as aristocrats! No. We will be hunters once more.
Before you is Safalaan Hallow, son of Efaritay Hallow. Her icyene blood runs through his veins. That blood contains the power to take us home.
We will never follow you, Drakan. Return to Vampyrium if you wish. Take those foolish enough to still believe in you as well if you like. The rest of us will remain here. This is our home now.
And how long will you last if you remain? The humans here are spent. There is no longer enough of them to feed you.
Then we must find a way to cross the Salve!
Many have tried and failed. Do you truly believe that you, Lord Myrmel, will have better luck?
No. There is only one hope for us now, but if you would rather die than accept that, then die you will.
With the blood of the half-icyene, I have been able to create a portal to travel to and from Vampyrium, but his blood alone isn't enough to transport us all. For that, more will be needed.
Human blood. Vampyre blood. It makes no difference. The half-icyene is the catalyst. The rest matters not. But one way or another, sacrifice will be required.
And how do you propose to achieve these sacrifices?
For that, fate seems to have already provided the answer. A blood moon will soon rise over these lands, and it will do so on the exact same night that one rises over Vampyrium.
And so, on that night, we shall finally hunt again, for at long last, we shall experience the Night of the Blood Moon once more.
The Night of the Blood Moon? You would bring back that festival?
Festival? A night of carnage would be a better description! You can't possibly believe we'll go along with this, Drakan!
If you will not hunt, you will be hunted. One way or another, the blood needed will be gathered.

You would see us go back to being mere beasts! We will not have it! You are a failure, Drakan. It's time we had a new leader. One who understands who we are now, rather than lamenting over what we once were.
If you wish for the title, then claim it. You know what the Night of the Blood Moon is. If by the night's end you have the most kills, Lord Myrmel, then you will become our leader.
Now, I must return to Vampyrium. There is much I need to prepare before the festival begins. The wise among you will begin to prepare as well.
As a starting point, you may wish to deal with the two humans that stand among you, unless of course you've all become so weak that you can't even do that anymore...
Are you okay, Ivan?
Yes... I'm fine... I'm sorry for... For what happened there.
It doesn't matter. I'm just glad you're okay.
I guess... I guess we need to start working on an evacuation plan. We need to get as many people out of Morytania as possible.
But how? We'll barely get anyone out in time.
I know, but what else can we do?
We stop Drakan! Stop him before he can begin this festival of his!

Stop Drakan?... I couldn't even cast a teleport spell to escape a few vyrewatch. Besides, even if we could stop him, you heard what he said. He's gone to this Vampyrium place. We can't get to him now.
There must be a way. Maybe we could make our own portal there? Or perhaps there's some existing form of teleportation we can use?
It sounded like it took Drakan years to work it out, and it only became possible thanks to Safalaan. Even if we could find a way, we don't have the time!
Well, how about we use the portal that Drakan's already made then?
But would that even work? The whole point of this festival is to gather the blood needed to use it.
True, but that's only so he can transport a large number of vampyres at once. He's presumably been using it himself without issue, so perhaps we can as well?
Perhaps... Say we're able to do this though. Say we manage to reach the portal and use it to get to Vampyrium. Then what?
Hmm...

I've got it! It's like you said: this is all only possible because of Safalaan! His blood is the catalyst! It doesn't matter how much other blood Drakan can gather. Without Safalaan, his whole plan is over!
Here's what we do: We find this portal, use it to travel to Vampyrium, find and rescue Safalaan, and then return here, closing the portal behind us when we do. Drakan would be left trapped there!
Meaning we'd never actually need to face him directly... I suppose it could work, but it's such a slim hope...
Maybe, but while there's still some hope, even slim, we can't give up.
Okay, let's say we do this... Where would we even start?
With more help. Drakan didn't quite kill all the Myreque.
You mean Veliaf? He abandoned us! What makes you think he'll suddenly help us now?
He might not, but we need to at least try to convince him.
We'd need to find him first.
Indeed. Any idea where he might have gone?
I never bothered looking into it much, given he didn't seem to care about checking on me.
But?
Last I spoke to Drezel, he mentioned hearing that Veliaf might be in Slepe.
Then let's get over there.

Fine. I need to make some arrangements here first, but then I'll head over there. If we end up getting separated, I've left a fair bit of equipment with Old Man Ral upstairs. Speak to him if you need anything.
Will do.
I'll meet you outside the church in Slepe. Oh, and...
Just make sure you've got your expectations in check. Even if we find Veliaf, be ready for him to disappoint us.
Hey, Ivan.
I'll be heading over to Slepe soon. I'll meet you outside the church there.
Alright, I'll see you there.
Ivan. Glad to see you made it okay.
And you. So where do we start?
Well, if Veliaf is here, someone must have seen him. We should ask around, and I reckon the pub will be the best place to start.
In that case, lead on.
Let's get going.
I'm right behind you.
Are you going to be okay when we find Veliaf?
I'll be fine. It's not like this is the first time Veliaf and I have had disagreements.
I feel like it's a bit more than just disagreements this time... Not to mention, we have no idea what sort of headspace he'll be in.
I've known him long enough that I could make a pretty good guess. For so long he tried his best to protect me... to protect all of us.
After what happened in Darkmeyer, he finally realised he couldn't, and it broke him. Veliaf often said I was naive, but in truth, I think he was always the naive one.
Anyway, it doesn't really matter. I may get why he left, but that doesn't change the fact that I might just hate him for it.
As for if I'll be okay when we find him? The truth is that I don't think I'll know until we do, so we may as well get to it.
I need to do something else.
Alright, I'll meet you back outside the church. Just don't take too long.
. Shall we get to it?
Indeed. I reckon the pub will be the best place to start.
Let's head over to the pub.
Good day,. Could I interest you in one of our finest Bloody Bracers? It's a local speciality.
We're looking for a friend of ours.
And you think this friend might have been here? Well, could you describe them?
I'd say he'd be best described as a complete and utter cretin.
Er... Yeah, he's a bit of a... grumpy fellow. He's also got black hair and a mustache.
Ah, yes I've seen him around. He was in here earlier in fact, having a drink...
Quite a bit to drink...
I see... You don't happen to know where he went after he left, do you?
That, I do not. However, I did hear that there was some commotion up at Crombwick Manor soon afterwards.
I suppose that could be worth a look. Thanks for the help.
It was very much my pleasure,.
Like I said, he left here after having quite a few drinks. I don't know where he went, but I did hear that there was some commotion up at Crombwick Manor soon afterwards.
Ah, yes. Thanks for the help.
Let's head over to Crombwick Manor.
Locked. We'll need to head through the dungeon.
What do you think you're doing?
Helping you.
Do I look like I need help?
With how drunk you are, I'd say the answer is yes. How many have you had?
Not enough. Now, if you're done asking stupid questions, would you mind getting out of my way?
Why? So you can run off again?
Run? Does it look like I'm running? Look around you! What do you see!
What I see is a drunk who's desperately trying to get himself killed!
You don't know what you're talking about!
Face it, Veliaf! You can spin things however you want, but the truth is, you abandoned us! You abandoned the Myreque!
The Myreque are gone, Ivan!
Not quite, Veliaf. Safalaan is still alive. Drakan has him as a prisoner, but we have a plan to save him.
What plan?
Drakan is using Safalaan's blood to travel to and from Vampyrium.
Vampyrium? What are you on about?
It's apparently the original home of the vampyres. It seems Safalaan's blood is essential to getting there.
So what? You want to go there and rescue him?
Pretty much. If we can bring Safalaan back, Drakan will end up trapped in Vampyrium.
You've gone mad! If Drakan has Safalaan, then he's as good as dead! We can't help him now. No one can!
So you'd just abandon him? I don't believe that!
Well, I abandoned you apparently! Maybe I was never the person you thought I was!
You were always the person I thought you were, Veliaf! You tried so hard to be the father I lost, and you know what, yes, you were terrible at it! But you tried, and that was enough for me!
I never lost faith in you! When you lied about Calsidiu, I understood why! Even when you lied about my parents, I understood why!
I never lied about your parents!
I'm not a fool, Veliaf! I know who my mother really was! I know I'm the descendant of Ivandis Seergaze!
? Did you tell him?
didn't need to tell me, Veliaf! I worked it out for myself! I was so angry when I did, but I forgave you, because I believed in you!
Maybe you've finally lost your faith in yourself, Veliaf. I'd understand if you have. Truth be told, I thought I'd lost my faith in you as well.
But now, standing here before you, I realise I haven't. Even after all that's happened! Even after all that you've done! I still believe in you!
Now, I'm going to Paterdomus. We need to work out how to reach Vampyrium. The library there seems like the best place to start.
You can stay here and drink yourself to death if you want, Veliaf, but this fight isn't over yet. I trust you'll make the right choice.
Right, anything you want to lecture me on?
Not really. Ivan put it better than I ever could. Now, I'd better get to Paterdomus.
Go on, get yourself to Paterdomus. No benefit to either of us you standing here talking to me.
... and this land you speak of... surely it can't actually exist?!
It seems it does, Drezel.
Ivan, please, do not go forward with this plan! I will send word to the King! He will send help, I'm sure of it!
Like his mercenaries? How useful have they been? Face it, Drezel, we're on our own.
Ah, ! Surely you are not in favour of this plan?
Well, it was actually my idea...
Oh, Saradomin save us...
Did Veliaf have anything else to say to you, ?
Not really.
Well, we'll just have to hope he makes the right choice. Anyway, now that you're here, we can get started.
What's the plan?
We need to find a way to reach this portal that Drakan has made. I reckon it's a pretty safe bet that it will be somewhere inside Castle Drakan.
Castle Drakan?! You have no hope of getting in there!
Not through the front door, but I'd be surprised if that was the only way in there.
Are you sure? Vanescula once said the castle was impenetrable.
But maybe she was lying, or maybe there are ways in even she didn't know about.
But how do we go about finding out?
Well, I had a look in the library and I found this old journal. Have a read of it and see what you reckon.
Have a read of that old journal, and see what you reckon.
So Ivandis set out to kill Drakan.
Exactly! He surely must have had some sort of plan for getting into the castle!
Apparently this squire hid Ivandis' writings within Paterdomus itself. Any idea what that might mean, Drezel?
Blasphemy! That's what it means! This journal clearly can't be trusted!
Maybe, but there's only one way to find out. Let's head up into the temple and see if we can find these writings.
I can't imagine those Zamorakians up there will just let us start poking around.
Well, I'd say they've well overstayed their welcome here anyway, so maybe it's about time we cleared them out.
Sounds like a plan! Let's do it!
I'm right behind you,.
You two be careful up there.
I won't be sad to see those Zamorakians gone, but just make sure you both take care up there.
Don't worry, Drezel, we will.
Let's go and deal with those Zamorakians.
Alright, I'll meet you back in the mausoleum. Just don't take too long.
Hmm... I should go and get Ivan before heading in there.
Right, now that those monks are dealt with, we can get to work on finding these writings. Any thoughts on where to start?
I'm not too sure, but I do wonder if that journal you found could help us out in some way. I'll give it another read and see what I can come up with.
Sounds good.
Could you remind me who the Seven Priestly Warriors were?
Sure thing. During the Fourth Age, Drakan and his vampyres tried to invade Misthalin. The Seven Priestly Warriors led the army that stood against him.
The war ended when the seven of them blessed the Salve, right here where Paterdomus was eventually built.
It's said that all seven died in the battle when the river was blessed, with them being buried in the mausoleum below.
Of course, as it turns out, that wasn't actually true. Ivandis survived the battle. He journeyed into Morytania and eventually died there.
And if this journal you found is to be believed, he did so while trying to kill Drakan.
Indeed.
What about the other six? Who were they?
There was Iriandul Caistlyn, Sarl Dunegun, Friar Twiblick, Derygull Templeton, Erysail the Pious and Essiandar Gar.
How did you find out you were descended from Ivandis?
Truth be told, I'm surprised I didn't work it out sooner. Drezel never hid the fact that he wanted me to succeed him, and he and Veliaf always tried so hard to keep me safe.
I always just thought they were trying to look out for me, but eventually I realised it was more than that. That there was something else going on.
I searched through the library below and found some information on Ivandis' family. It took some work, but I was eventually able to link them directly to my mother, and to me.
Why didn't you tell us that you knew?
At first I was angry, but I soon came to understand why. By that point though, there was no easy way to bring it up, and let's be honest, we often had more important things to worry about.
Very true.
I'll get to it.
Any ideas so far?
Not yet.
Keep at it.
! Over here!
Well?
This is... quite something. Here, you'd better see for yourself.
So Ivandis started to become a vampyre...
He gave everything to stop them, and that was his reward... I can't even begin to imagine what that must have been like...
In a weird way though, it kind of gives me hope. Ivandis may have died before he could kill Drakan, but thanks to him, we might now be able to succeed where he failed.
So many people have died in this fight. Ivandis was one of thousands. But if their sacrifices can help us succeed now, then they didn't die for nothing.
Now, let's head back down to the mausoleum. Maybe best we don't mention Ivandis becoming a vampyre to Drezel...
Veliaf! You've...
Sobered up?
Well, that's one way of putting it...
Veliaf, about earlier...
We'll talk about it later. In the meantime, Drezel tells me you've been working on some suicide plan to reach Vampyrium. Come on, let's hear it.
Before he died, Ivandis Seergaze set out on one final attempt to kill Drakan. It seems he was aware of a tunnel leading directly into Castle Drakan.
We find this tunnel, use it to enter the castle, take Drakan's portal to Vampyrium, rescue Safalaan, then return through the portal, closing it behind us.
Yup, suicide...
So where's this tunnel?
Given this was meant to be Ivandis' last act before his death, my guess would be within the caves where I found his tomb.
Alright then, I guess we'd better get going.
Can you not wait a bit longer? I sent a letter to the King!
And I'm sure he'll send us his best wishes in return. Face it, Drezel, as far as everyone in Misthalin is concerned, Morytania is a lost cause.
Truth be told, they're probably right. In a few hours, we'll almost certainly all be dead.
Very inspiring...
Well, if you wanted inspiration, you shouldn't have come up with a suicide mission. Now let's go.
Lead the way.
So here we are. The final resting place of Ivandis Seergaze. I'm not seeing any tunnel anywhere...
Let's have a look around and see what we can find.
I'll make my own way there.
Fair enough. Just let us know if you change your mind.
I wish you wouldn't go ahead with this plan, but it seems you've made your decision. Please though, be careful, and make sure you take good care of Ivan.
I will, Drezel. I promise.
No point wasting any time. Let's go and investigate those caves.
Find anything, ?
There's some sort of collapsed tunnel here. I reckon I'm going to need to go get a pickaxe and then try mining through it.
You didn't bring a pickaxe with you?
No.
Even though you knew we were going to an underground cave? Some adventurer you are!
Well, I only have so much space to carry things.
Good job I brought one then! Just come grab it if you need it.
Here's that pickaxe,.
Thanks! I'll get to work.
Any luck with that tunnel?
I'm still working on it.
Well, keep at it.
Any luck?
Maybe... I reckon there might be something behind that wall over there. I'm going to try and mine through it.
Well, let us know how it goes.
Best we keep moving,.
Are you okay?
Yes... Thank you...
What is this place?
They make us refine the daeyalt here. They use it to make more vampyres!
More vampyres? But why? Why are they still making more when they're already suffering from overcrowding?
I'm sorry, but I don't know...
Well, you don't need to worry about them any longer. You're free now. Head through the tunnel we came through. You'll find a route leading towards Canifis. Head to Paterdomus once you get there.
Thank you!
We'd better keep moving. It probably won't be long before someone comes to check in on things here.
I reckon we're getting close now,. Lead the way.
We can't be far off now. Stay alert.
I think this might be it,.
This must be it. Keep a close eye out for vampyres.
I guess this is it...
We've no idea what we'll find on the other side. If we get separated, try to make your way back to the portal.
That's assuming Drakan himself doesn't rip us to shreds as soon as we arrive...
What a lovely thought. No point in us waiting around I guess. Let's do this...
Did it work?
Veliaf?!
Eugh...
I'm fine.
If you're sure...
Did something go wrong? This room looks very similar to the one we just left...
I don't think so... I reckon we're in another Castle Drakan. I guess Drakan based the one in Morytania on this one.
We came through a dungeon to get into the one in Morytania. If this one matches that, then I bet that's where Safalaan is.
Then let's get down there!
Wait! Do you hear that?
! Run!
Veliaf! Are you okay?
I'm fine. Any sign of Ivan?
Afraid not. I'm sure he'll find us though. He knows the dungeon is the aim and he knows where the portal is as well.
Hmm... Best we keep progressing on then.
Any thoughts on what to do next?
Not really. There's something off about these portraits though...
Do you think things will be okay between you and Ivan?
Is now really the best time for this?
Well, as you keep pointing out, there's a high chance of us dying here, so we might not get another chance.
So you're saying this is my opportunity to clear my conscience and die content?
Maybe not exactly how I'd have put it...
Well, given we're almost certainly dead anyway, I don't see how it matters anymore.
Oh, come on. If you really believe that, why bother coming here at all?
Why? Because I failed! I failed to protect the Myreque! I failed to protect Ivan! I made one promise to his mother, and I broke it!
But Ivan's still alive! This isn't over yet!
This was over the second we agreed to Vanescula's plan! Now all of us are living on borrowed time. Me, you, Ivan, Safalaan... None of us are getting out of this alive.
So the only reason you came here is so you wouldn't have to die alone and drunk?
Pretty much.
I don't believe that, and deep down I don't think you do either.
Believe what you want,. It won't matter soon anyway.
Agreed. Let's go.
Stay alert. Drakan could be anywhere.
Safalaan! Are you okay?
Who... Who are you? What is this?
What's wrong with him?
Vanescula! What did your brother do to him?

Good to see you both as well. Now, in case you hadn't noticed, my brother and I aren't exactly on the best of terms right now. As for what happened to Safalaan, you tell me. He's been like this since he arrived.
It must be because of what happened with Vanstrom.
What do we do with him?
First, we need to get him out of here.
I take it you have a plan?
There's a portal back to Morytania upstairs. We can use it to escape.
And what happens when we're back in Morytania? What happens when my brother finds we're no longer in his dungeon?
It doesn't matter. We'll close the portal behind us. Without Safalaan, he'll be trapped here.
Ah, I see you've thought through this plan well. You have however missed just the one very minor detail.
That being?
My brother comes down here periodically to collect blood from Safalaan. He must be stockpiling it.
Then we need to destroy this stockpile. Where will it be?
My brother's private chambers are on the top floor of the castle. My guess would be somewhere up there.
Alright, you two get Safalaan back to Morytania. I'll find Ivan, destroy the stockpile and then follow you.
Leave you here alone? No chance!
Safalaan is the priority!
And unless you destroy that stockpile, he'll be no safer on that side of the portal than this one. We're staying.
Fine, but if there's any sign of danger, you don't wait for me. Use the portal and get out right away.
Now, let's not waste any time. Drakan is around here somewhere. It's only a matter of time before he finds us. We need to be gone before that happens.
Best you get to it,. I'll keep an eye on things here.
Any thoughts on what I should do now?
I guess you should check the rooms we didn't go into earlier. One of them might give you a way forward.
Hopefully I'll find Ivan in one of them as well.
Yeah... hopefully.
I'll get going.
I don't... I don't understand. What's happening?
Everything's going to be okay, Safalaan. I promise.
Okay...
Unless you fancy facing my brother, I'd suggest you get a move on and destroy that blood stockpile.
What do you make of your brother's plan?
I must confess, I underestimated him. I thought he'd long since given up on... well, anything and everything really. Now I see the reality was far worse.
We lost some good people thanks to your underestimating.
Well, I hope you're not expecting an apology. You all knew what you were signing up for.
I see your time in the cells hasn't changed you.
And why would it have? This is not my first time on the back foot. I survived all those previous times, and I will survive this time as well.
If you say so. Anyway, back to your brother's plan...
Yes, like I say, rather unexpected, though I must admit, it is somewhat inspired.
How so?
When we took Hallowvale, Lowerniel said it would be a new beginning for us, but it only took him a few hundred years to grow bored of that.
That's when he started lamenting about this place instead. He longed to find a way back here, and for a time he actually found one.
He worked out how to get here before? How?
I don't know exactly. My brother was once entrusted with a powerful artefact. I did wonder if that might have been connected, but the timelines don't add up...

Anyway, however he did it, it didn't last. He eventually lost his way to get here. After that, he mostly withdrew from our society completely. I thought he'd given up, but now I suspect it was all part of a larger plan.
I don't think he ever stopped trying to find a way back here, and I think he was already preparing for the day when he'd work out how to do so.
You saw for yourself how my people responded to his announcement. I think it's fair to say that the prospect of returning to Vampyrium is not one that many take joy in.
And yet... some might consider it more appealing than it once would have been.
The overcrowding... The shutting down of the Haemalchemy Laboratory... I think he was intentionally pushing us to the brink. Putting us in a place where his plan seemed like the only option.
Hmm... Before we came here, we found a vampyrification lab. We did wonder why new vampyres were being made given the overcrowding issues.
Yes, especially given my brother's hatred for that process. A process he himself made I should point out. Still, I suppose hypocrisy has always been one of his many talents.
What do you know about this festival your brother is planning?
Ah, yes, the wonderful Night of the Blood Moon. It was once the way that the Drakan clan chose their new leaders. This was before the vampyre clans were united as one. Before we became civilised.
I'm not sure I could ever describe a vampyre as civilised.

Well, then you should be glad you never had to see how we used to live. That festival is a perfect example of something that should have remained forgotten, but of course, my brother can't help but cling to the past.
So this festival is how your brother became leader?
Yes. We were a lot more superstitious back then, though a lot stupider might be a better way to put it. We believed that a blood moon was the ultimate representation of power.
Whenever one occurred, the festival would take place. It was a whole night of killing. The one with the most kills by the end was said to embody the blood moon.
Embody the blood moon?
'And when dawn comes, one will rise above all, and they will rise as the Blood Moon.'
Like I said, we were stupid back then, and not overly creative. The victor would be granted the rather uninspired title of Blood Moon. They were the only one deemed worthy enough to lead the clan.
And now your brother wants to bring the festival back.
He'll do anything but accept the truth. All of our problems... they come from him. He will never be the one to free us of them.
What can you tell me about this land?
It's a wretched place. Leaving was the best thing we ever did.
Why? What was life like here?
Well, it was once the case that my people lived in separate clans spread across these lands. Life was short and brutal. There was nothing to take joy in. Survival was all that mattered.
What changed?

A single visitor. We called him the Stranger from Afar. He uplifted us. He showed us that life could be more than mere survival. You wouldn't think it now, but back then my brother was his biggest believer.
As you can probably imagine, such a fundamental shift in our society caused quite the stir, but also presented opportunities to those willing to take them...
My brother was one of those people. He set out to unite all the clans as one, with him as their leader. He called himself the Lord of Vampyrium, the first true ruler of these lands.
This Stranger from Afar... did he support that?
More than support it. He enabled it. Make no mistake though, it was not due to any benevolence. He had great ambition of his own, but he needed us to help him achieve it.
And so, we remained here for centuries after that, enjoying our new lives of culture and civilisation, until eventually the Stranger from Afar returned.
He guided us to your lands. There, we established a great empire for him, and for hundreds of years, we prospered. Vampyrium became nothing more than a horrible distant memory.
You see, after all this time, it seems my brother has forgotten something that he once knew better than anyone. Change is inevitable, and those who refuse to accept it, die.
I'll get back to it.
Ivan! Thank goodness you're okay!
! Thank you! If you hadn't shown up when you did...
Look at me... I don't belong here...
None of us do, Ivan.
Did you... find Veliaf?
Yes, and we've managed to rescue Safalaan and Vanescula as well. They're waiting downstairs.
Is Safalaan okay?
He's... alive. I think for now that's the best we can hope for.
Hmm... Okay. Well, let's head down there then and get out of here.
Not yet. Drakan has a stockpile of Safalaan's blood up in his chambers. It needs destroying before we can leave.
Okay... In that case, lead the way.
I'm not sure, but I wonder if there's more to some of these books than there first seems.
Are you doing okay, Ivan?
I don't know. I'm alive I guess, but I keep letting you down,. I'm sorry.
Don't be. I'm sorry that you have to be here, Ivan, but I'm glad you are. I wouldn't have got this far on my own.
I just wish I could be more like you and Veliaf. I thought I could be, but after what happened to the others...
The worst part is, I can't even mourn them. After Sani died, and Harold... I felt something. Now though... now I just feel empty. Empty... and afraid.
And yet you're still here. Even after all that's happened, you haven't lost hope, Ivan.
Yeah... hope. That's always been me, hasn't it. The hoper... The believer... But what good is hope now? What good has hope ever done us? It's just... worthless.
No. It's worth everything. It's the only reason we're still here, and it's the reason why I know that no matter what we'll face here, we'll win.
You know, you're pretty good at this whole motivation thing. Much better than Veliaf.
Well... that's not saying much.
He has his moments.
That he most certainly does.
Let's go.
We'd better keep going,
I found some supplies,. Just let me know if you need them.
I'm not sure. I guess we need to work out how to get to that blood stockpile. Hopefully it won't take us too long. I don't want to spend any longer here than we have to.
Could I have those supplies you found?
Sure.
Thanks.
We'd better keep going,.
Ivan!
Veliaf.
May I suggest you save the reunions for later. We need to focus on getting out of here.
This must be it.
There. Drakan should have no way of making a new portal now.
Good. Let's get out of here.
Uh oh...
Vanescula? What are you doing up here?
Well, given you'd been gone for a while, I thought I'd best come make sure my brother hadn't found you.
Now, I take it the blood stockpile is destroyed?
It is.
Then it would be wise for us to leave. Come.
Let's save the reunions for later. We need to get out of here.
After all these years, I have found that life has become so... monotonous.
Take my sister here. There was once a time when I found elation in her little plots. Over time however, elation became boredom. Eventually, boredom became indifference.
This little foray of yours, however... I confess, it has me moderately impressed.
This bravery... This defiance! It brings back a taste that's become all too absent back in Morytania. To finally find it again, here in Vampyrium... How fitting indeed.
What's it to be then, brother? Back to the cells with us? Or will you do us the kindness of killing us here and being done with it?
Vanescula, my dear sister, you never fail to disappoint. Have you truly become so despondent, that even mere humans now offer more tenacity than you.
Oh, I assure you, brother, I still have plenty of fire within me.
Good. Then let us put it to the test.
You're toying with us!
I'm offering you a choice. If you wish for your freedom, it's right out there waiting for you.
You...
Vanescula...
Let's go. Now!
Let the hunt begin.
What's the plan here, Vanescula?
We need to get across the bridge. We can't stay here.
Where even is here?
Sangvesti. This was our home once. After Lowerniel united the vampyre clans, this is where we lived.
This is where we truly became who we are now. Art... Culture... The things my brother now hates. They all came from him.
Yeah, very touching, but given he's going to be upon us any minute, maybe less reminiscing and more action!
How do we get the bridge down?
It's probably not been used for thousands of years. The mechanism's going to need repairing.
How long will that take?
Were you under the impression that during my time in my brother's dungeon, I decided to take up engineering? I have no idea how long it will take!
It looks like one of the cogs is missing...
Well, we're not going to get very far without it.
I'll find it.
But it could be anywhere!
We don't have any other option. The rest of you stay here. Get the other parts of the mechanism fixed, and make sure Safalaan is kept safe.
You know Drakan's going to be out there, right?
Then I'll just have to avoid him.
Well, it's safe to say I've had better days. It's not looking good for us at all.
No, but this isn't over yet. We'll work something out.
I hope you're right.
Would you be able to look after some things for me?
Sure. I'll make sure they get back to your bank... provided we ever get back to Morytania...
I'd best get going.
Just be careful out there.
Where am I? What's going on?
Don't worry, Safalaan. We'll be out of here soon.
I hope so...
Veliaf.
How's Safalaan doing?
Well, he's alive, but otherwise, not great. He doesn't seem to remember anything.
Is this what happened to him before? The last time he fully lost control of his powers?
I think so. I never saw him for myself in those early days, but this is exactly how Vertida described it.
There must be something we can do for him once we're back in Morytania.
We never worked out a way before. He never regained the memories he lost.
True, but we can't give up on him.
Well, we need to survive this first, and with us now having no clear way back to Morytania, the odds of that happening are even slimmer than before.
Slim perhaps, but not hopeless.
If you say so.
Have you found that cog?
Well, probably best you work on that, given we'll surely soon be dead without it.
I found the cog.
Good. Let's finish getting this thing fixed and then let's get out of here.
And then what? What's the plan here?
We need to put more distance between us and the castle. Once we're far enough away, we can double back and hopefully make a new portal.
Hopefully?
Do you have any better ideas?
Maybe we leave you here as a distraction while we escape? After all, this entire mess is of your making.
What a fantastic idea, Veliaf! Yes, why not kill the only person who actually knows their way around this place. Brilliant as always!
We don't have time for this. Whatever we do next, we can't stay here. Let's get across that bridge.
Before we go, Ivan found some supplies. Best you speak to him and stock up,.
We shouldn't waste any more time here.
Agreed. Let's get going.
Do you remember this place, Vanescula?
All too well.
This was our real home. Not that town back there, or that castle. This here is the last place we were truly who we were meant to be.
And who was it who changed all that, brother?
My greatest mistake. One that will finally be put right. At long last, the blood moon will rise once more, and when it does, we will finally reclaim the greatness that we lost.
Greatness? I remember it a bit differently. Fear, suffering and carnage. That was what life was like here.
Yes, and it was beautiful.

It was barbaric! Thousands of years have passed and yet I still remember what happened here like it was yesterday! I remember looking on as our father sat right where you are now, with you stood over him!
Just as he wanted. He dreamed of the day when I would succeed him.
I was a child! I was a child who had to stand and watch as my father died!
Our father died in glory! He fought on the Night of the Blood Moon and fell as a warrior!
A warrior? Is that what you tell yourself? You killed him like he was a mere animal! A mere beast!
We've always been beasts, Vanescula, and no matter how much you try to hide it, that's all we ever will be.
Ivan! Protect Safalaan!
Now's our chance! Let's get out of here!
Where do we go?!
Deeper into the forest! Quick!
Ivan?
Veliaf?
I must confess human, you fight well. It is rare for one of your kind to display the skill that you have.
I'm not here to impress you. I'm here to stop you. We won't be plagued by your evil any longer!
Evil? If only it were that simple.
That simple? You're responsible for the deaths of thousands! You keep humans as slaves! As cattle!
And does the farmer quarrel with the cattle?
You are no farmer! And we are no cattle!
Don't misunderstand me human, for I agree with you. What we did to your kind... at the time it seemed so necessary...
In truth, however, the day we stopped being hunters and started being farmers is the day we lost who we were. That is why I will bring an end to it.
Surely you must understand that I am the only one that offers hope for your kind. If I get my way, there will be no more vampyres in Morytania. Your people will finally be free once more.
But how many will have to die first for that to happen? How many dead humans will power that portal of yours? It's too high a cost!
There's always a cost. The weak must die so that the strong may survive. It is how every race operates, even yours. There is no alternative.
There's always an alternative!
And what is yours? Vanescula? What do you think she would have done had her plan to kill me succeeded? What would her answer have been to the blood shortages?
She already had one. Before you shut it down, the Haemalchemy Laboratory beneath Meiyerditch was already researching ways to overcome the shortages. That was her answer.
You believe it was I who shut that lab down? How misguided you are. It was Vanescula who put an end to their research. She has never had any desire to see that work succeed.
I don't believe you!
Then don't. It makes no difference to me. You are nothing more than a distraction. A passing amusement while I prepare to restore our people to glory.
The Night of the Blood Moon approaches, and while I have enjoyed this little diversion, I have more important things to focus on.
Come with me! Now!
Are you alright?
I'm fine... but, your companions... Shouldn't we go back and help them?
No. They will already be dead.
But... Who are you?
My name is Efaritay.
Efaritay Hallow? Your Safalaan's mother! But how are you here? How are you alive?
I was Drakan's prisoner here for many years, until I made my escape, but we can discuss this further inside.
Wait! Safalaan and the others are still out there!
You do not need to worry. Both my son and your friends are safe. Now let us go. There is someone who will want to meet you.
! Thank goodness you're okay!
Ivan! Veliaf! It's good to see you.
We thought we'd lost you back there,.
If it wasn't for these people, we probably would have. They saved all of us!
But who are they? The ones in the hoods... I've seen people like that before, back in Morytania.
It seems the answer to that is... complicated.
How do you mean?
Probably best you talk to them yourself.
And so we properly meet at last. Greetings, my child. I'm glad to see you are safe.
I think that's the first time I've ever heard anything like that from a vampyre.
Yes... I understand your experiences with my kind are likely to give you a... less than warm feeling towards me.
However, I think you'll soon find that when it comes to your kind, I take a slightly different perspective to other vampyres.
Okay...
I must say, I'm glad to finally be able to speak with you in person, though I appreciate the circumstances are... less than ideal.
In person... But that must mean... The hooded stranger at the Theatre of Blood! You're their master!
Indeed. I've been called many things over the years, but to you, my child, I am Sugadinti. Sugadinti Vitur.
Vitur? As in Verzik Vitur?
My daughter.
Oh...
You need not worry. My daughter betrayed me long ago. When I rejected Lowerniel Drakan's attempts to unite my clan with his, she chose to conspire with him.

She made an attempt on my life, leaving me for dead, before claiming my clan and title as her own. To learn that she eventually met her end due to one of her own creations... I must admit, I found that rather pleasing...
I see...
It is unfortunate that betrayal comes so naturally to our kind. I'm sorry that you yourself fell victim to that.
What do you mean?

Your companion, Vanescula. She was so eager for you to help her overthrow her brother, and yet, it seems her plans for you and your companions were not as... altruistic as she might have had you believe.
We found her while we were searching for you. We also found this on her. It is not a substance that occurs naturally here. We assume she obtained it at some point during your escape.
Daeyalt? But why?
Why indeed? Mid way through a daring and dangerous escape, and she goes out of her way to aquire a key component for vampyrification, yet elects not to tell you. Curious...
Still, you need not fear, for she is no longer a danger to you. I have her imprisoned in the dungeon below.
But I don't understand... Vanescula helped us escape. We wouldn't be here if not for her.
No, you helped Vanescula escape. Make no mistake, you'd have been dead the moment she no longer needed you.
Indeed... However, I suggest we not dwell on it, for there are more pressing matters to discuss.
Her brother?
Yes... This palace here was once the home of the late Lord Jovkai. It has served us well as a hideout for some time, and we have done a commendable job of keeping our presence here hidden.
But now we've revealed ourselves, meaning Drakan will come for us. We need to leave.
I take it you have a plan?
That we do. I suspect it to be the same plan that you yourself had.
Drakan is flesh and blood like any other foe, but he is not one that will be defeated easily. However, his defeat is not required for us to be victorious.
So a portal?

Precisely, my child. We may not have the resources of Drakan, but we have been preparing for the day when we will travel to Hallowvale for some time. You yourself have been of great assistance with some of those efforts.
You're talking about the hooded figures?
My loyal disciples, the aranei. Their presence in Hallowvale has served two purposes.
Not only have they been laying the groundwork for our eventual arrival, but they have also been helping us to perfect the haemalchemy needed to sustain the portal that we require.
And you're now ready to make that portal?
Some final preparation will be needed first, but yes.
And if Drakan arrives before it's ready?
My disciples... They have already started making preparations for that eventuality. Whilst I attend to the final work needed for the portal, you may wish to assist them.
I suppose I can do that.
There is concern in your voice. You do not trust me.
I guess this is all just a lot to take in, and as you said yourself, it's not like I've had good experiences with your kind.

Nor have I, but if not for Sugadinti, I would never have survived these lands. I'm afraid you have no choice but to put your faith in him. If you do not, we are almost certainly doomed. Now, let us get to work.
We are still preparing everything we need to make the portal, my child. While we do, may I suggest you assist my disciples and your companions with their own preparations.
I wanted to ask you something.
Yes... I imagine you have many questions. I assure you that I will answer them all, but for now we must focus on current matters.
Hmm... Fair enough.
I'll do just that.
Good. I will let you know once we are ready here.
If you need anything at all, friend, just speak with Father Sugadinti.
I am glad to finally meet you, friend. I have heard many good things about you.
Greetings, my friend. It is good to have you here with us.
I am sorry you and your companions had to face Lord Drakan alone. We thank Father Sugadinti that you survived.
Greetings, my friend. Father Sugadinti has asked me to look after some of your items, if that is something that will be of benefit to you?
Yes please.
No thanks.
As you wish.
My child, you have suffered so much... All these years apart... All the time we've lost...
I'm sorry to disturb you... er...
You may simply call me Efaritay.
It's an honour, Efaritay.
Thank you, but your honour is not needed. I'm not a queen anymore.
Maybe not, but all these years later, Queen Efaritay is still remembered in Morytania. Even with all that's happened, your name still brings hope to those that live there.
They'd do well to find a better source of hope, but I suppose that isn't important now. There is a lot to be done, but first, my son needs tending to.
Anything I can do to help?
I'm preparing a potion that should help him, but he also needs to eat. If you head outside, you will find an amitire plant I have been cultivating.
Take some leaves from it and then mix them into a stew. We are not the best supplied here, but I'm sure you will find the ingredients around here to make one.
Alright, I'll get to it.
Greetings, my friend.
Is everything okay out here?
For now, but we must be ready for Lord Drakan to arrive at any time. Many of my fellow disciples are out in the forest, keeping watch for him. They will send word as soon as he is sighted.
They're out there right now? How will they get back in time?
They most likely won't.
And they're okay with that?

It is the highest honour. They are out there because Father Sugadinti himself chose them personally. To die in his name, fighting to ensure the defeat of Lord Drakan... it is the kind of death we all dream of.
It just seems so... brutal.
This land is brutal. Most of us die before we've ever had the chance to live. In truth, our people should have died out long ago. It is only thanks to Father Sugadinti that we didn't.
So now you'll die for him?
Of course. We owe everything to him. Every moment... every experience... every memory. We exist because of him, and so we exist for him.
He is our future, and if we have to die to protect that future, then we will do so willingly.
I kind of understand... It just still seems so... extreme.
You are wise to be doubtful, but if the thousands of years our kind have spent here have taught us one thing, it is that this is the only way.
Well, hopefully that doesn't have to be the case for much longer.
With Father Sugadinti guiding us, I am certain that will be so.
... Is that you?
It's me. I'm here, Safalaan.
Thank you... for not giving up on me.
Never.
We should let him rest.
He was more lucid there. Is he recovering?
It was likely only temporary. A result of the potion I gave him. However, it is a first step. Given time, the Safalaan you knew will return. I'm sure of it.
Now, we must focus on ensuring we are prepared for Drakan.
I imagine you have more experience with him than most. Any recommendations?
All I can tell you about him is that he's a monster. He kept me alive in that castle of his, using my blood to travel to and from these lands.

And for all those years, with each and every day, he tormented me with false hope. He told me my daughter was alive. He told me my husband was alive. It was only after I escaped that I discovered the truth.
I was with Safalaan when he found out what happened. I'm so sorry for what he did to you, Efaritay.
Let us not dwell on the past. It is the present that requires our focus. On that note, while I may not have much advance on Drakan, I do have some suggestions regarding that weapon of yours.
My flail?
Indeed. I see you have used blisterwood as part of its construction. I'm glad to see my old tree is still serving a use.
If not for that tree, I think I'd probably be dead by now.
I'm glad to hear it, but blisterwood is not the only thing effective against vampyres. I take it you have noticed the spear Drakan carries?
I have. I must say, it doesn't look like a particularly vampyric weapon.
That's because it's not. It's called the Sunspear and I made it myself from blisterwood and pure silvthrill. It was one of the many things Drakan took from me.
Drakan uses a blisterwood weapon? Does that not hurt him?
Almost certainly, but Drakan will no doubt see his ability to push through that as a clear sign of his strength.
Anyway, the reason I brought up that spear is because of the other component used to make it.
Silvthrill?
Not just any silvthrill. Pure silvthrill. The smiths of Hallowvale were able to perfect the process of creating the alloy, making it far more powerful than the crude form used in your flail.
Unfortunately, the secrets to that process have long been lost, but pure silvthrill can still be found, provided you know where to look.
Hallowed marks. The old currency of Hallowvale. When Sugadinti and I first managed to send one of his disciples to my former home, I made sure that gathering these was their first priority.
Doing so required them to desecrate the tombs of my people. To have to resort to such methods...
In any case, thanks to their efforts, we have been able to gather enough pure silvthrill to create new weapons with. I would suggest you use it to enhance your flail.
I'll do that.
While doing so, may I also suggest some other improvements?
The main shaft of the flail seems quite cumbersome. If you were to shorten it, it would likely make the weapon quicker to strike with.
I also see you've used enchanted gems as part of the construction. I'd recommend that while shortening the shaft, you replace the sickle with one containing an enchanted diamond.
Don't happen to have any diamonds lying around, do you?
I believe you should be able to find one over in the armoury, along with everything else you'll need.
Let me know if you need a hand with anything, but otherwise, I now need to move onto my own preparations.
How did you end up allying with Sugadinti?
After I managed to escape Drakan, I was alone and weak. I would not have survived these lands for long, but I was lucky enough that Sugadinti found me.
That feels kind of like what happened with us.
Yes, and much like yourselves, I was also highly mistrusting of Sugadinti at first. Had I been stronger, I may well have tried to kill him on the spot.
And yet, over time, we have come to reach an understanding. Make no mistake, there is much we do not agree on. However, he is most certainly nothing like Drakan.
That's reassuring. Thank you.
I assume it's your blood we're using for this portal?
It is.
Will it be powerful enough for all of us? Drakan's been planning this Night of the Blood Moon festival to gather the blood for his.
Sugadinti's disciples have been providing their blood for it as well. You need not fear. We have more than enough to ensure everyone here can use it.
Are they happy providing their blood?
They are. I do not deny that their relationship with Sugadinti is complicated, and it is not one I totally approve of.
However, it is a relationship that they are content with, and it has worked for them for thousands of years.
Fair enough. So after we use the portal, what then?
That is something that still has an element of debate to it.
Until recently, our plan was to remain here in Vampyrium until we were strong enough to defeat Drakan, but recent events have made that impossible.
And we're the ones responsible for those recent events. I'm sorry.

You are not to blame. In hindsight, we should have revealed ourselves to you. At the time though, it seemed too risky. We did not want there to be any chance of Drakan and his kin learning about our plans.
But now those plans have changed. Drakan won't be defeated anymore. He'll just be trapped here instead. I'm guessing that's where the debate is?

Yes... Trapping Drakan here in the short term makes perfect sense, but the question is what do we do about him in the longer term. Sugadinti believes that once trapped here, he will have no hope of escape.
That was our hope as well, but I'm guessing you disagree?
How can we be sure he won't find a way? Even if not him, what happens if someone one day works out how to open a new portal to Vampyrium? While he lives, how can this truly be over?
Hmm... You make a fair point.
But do I? Is it logic that drives these questions, or is it something else...?

There is nothing left of who I once was. Drakan took everything from me, but then wouldn't even grant me the mercy of death. And now, all these years later, I find myself asking, what is it I'm still fighting for?
I tell myself it's for the future. A future for my son... A future for all who have suffered at the hands of the vampyres...

Once I would have prayed to Saradomin for that to be true... For a part of the old me to still remain... But he stopped listening to my prayers long ago. Now I wonder if deep down, only one thing drives me now...
Vengeance.
Let us speak of something else.
Do you mind if I ask about your family?
I'd... prefer you didn't.
I understand. I'm sorry to have mentioned them.
Could you tell me more about Hallowvale?
Hallowvale... The truth is, it's been so long that I barely remember it. The one memory that will never fade though, is the beauty of it.
The rivers and the forests... The cities of blue and white stone... And looking over all of it, Everlight.
Everlight?
Hallowvale wasn't always our home. My people once lived eternally in the light, in a floating city that followed the sun. We couldn't do that in Hallowvale, so we built a sun of our own.
I suppose you could compare it to a lighthouse. It stood on the outskirts of our capital, ensuring that no part of our home fell into darkness.
That sounds incredible.
It was... but now it's all gone. Sugadinti's disciples tell me nothing remains of Everlight now, nor much else of Hallowvale. Even its name has long since been lost to time.
But you're still here, and so is Safalaan. The light hasn't fully died yet, and for as long as we keep fighting, it never will.
I suppose we'll soon find out if you're right.
I upgraded my flail like you suggested.
It's been a long time since I've seen a weapon crafted in this way. It's like a small part of Hallowvale is right here with us. It's... beautiful.
But now is not the time to admire it. Drakan will be here soon and there is still much to prepare.
In that case, I shall leave you to it.
Hey, Ivan. Doing okay?
On the whole, I suppose. I really thought we were done for out there though, and now to find out about all of this... It's a lot to take in.
You can say that again.
This is Sarei, by the way. Apparently the two of you have met before?
Indeed we have. It was here who assisted Father Sugadinti and I in the Theatre of Blood. Your work was very impressive.
Thank you.
Though it does beg the question... What was this work? All this time we've been fighting Drakan, and now we learn your kind were there as well. Why didn't you help?
Your doubt is understandable. However, you must understand that from our perspective, you did not need help.
What do you mean?
Our presence in Morytania has always been highly limited. When Father Sugadinti first started sending us, he had not yet perfected the haemalchemy needed to do so. Many of our kind died as a result.
That's horrible!
Yes, but their sacrifices were necessary. It is only thanks to them that he and the icyene can now make a portal capable of taking us all to Morytania.
I'm sorry, I didn't realise... I still don't understand what you mean by us not needing help though.
Due to our limited presence, we had to prioritise our efforts carefully. Our numbers were too low for direct action, so we were limited to either spying or recruiting locals to assist us.
At the request of the icyene, we did our best to keep an eye on your group, but given you had managed to kill Ranis Drakan, it did not seem that you were in need of immediate assistance.
Of course, had we known you were working with Vanescula, we would have acted differently, but by the time we found out, it was already too late.
That makes sense. I'm sorry for doubting you, Sarei.
Your apology is not required. Trust is earned, not given. We are strangers to you, and Father Sugadinti is of the same race as your mortal foe.
Speaking of which, allow me to impart some knowledge to you both that may be of benefit to you in the likely event that you find yourself facing that foe again.
The icyene was hoping to cultivate a new blisterwood tree here, but was unfortunately unsuccessful. However, we were able to acquire a small amount of blisterwood from Darkmeyer for her.
While not as effective as your flail, you might find it beneficial to craft some stakes from this blisterwood. You can use them like a throwing knife, allowing you to harm vampyres from a distance.
I'd advise you make yourself some. You can do so using the blisterwood logs from the crate in the corner.
Thanks!
Do not mention it.
I guess you'd better make yourself some of those stakes,.
Has anything come of our work in the Theatre, Sarei?
I believe so, but you will need to speak to Father Sugadinti if you wish to know the specifics.
What exactly was it you were doing there, anyway?
Preparing. Lady Vitur was a longtime ally of Lord Drakan, and very much a foe to Father Sugadinti. For his eventual arrival in Morytania to go smoothly, he required that she be dealt with.
Only as it turns out, she already had been.
Yes, Sugadinti said something similar to us when we first arrived. I must admit, I don't really understand that bit. What happened?
Verzik bit off more than she could chew with her nylocas breeding program. She bred a queen nylocas, only for it to kill her and secretly take her place.
An unexpected turn of events. However, thanks to our work in the Theatre, Father Sugadinti now has plans for this Nylocas Queen.
As for what those plans are, as I say, you'll need to ask Father Sugadinti.
Hey,. Did you make some of those stakes?
You'll find the blisterwood in a crate in the corner.
Hey,.
I made some of those stakes.
Good. I hope you find them useful.
I hope so too. We're going to need all the advantages we can find.
Finally where she belongs.
So you think Sugadinti's right about her?
Right? I doubt that. He's a vampyre, and one thing we most certainly should have learnt by now is that vampyres can't be trusted.
But if we can't trust him, then why should we believe what he has to say about Vanescula?
We shouldn't. Make no mistake, he has his own reasons for wanting Vanescula out of the picture. However, that doesn't change the fact that she is our enemy. She has always been our enemy.
Hmm... You might be right, but we should try to find out for sure.
Well, if you want to try getting something out of her, be my guest.
Ah,. Come to gloat?
Gloat? I'm not the one that did this to you.
But you seem more than happy to be friends with the one that did. He's quite something, Sugadinti. I still remember how we celebrated when we thought he'd finally been dealt with.
Would you like to hear some stories about him?
I'd prefer you tell me about that daeyalt. Why? Why waste time stealing it when we were working on our escape?
Call it insurance.
Insurance for what?
You should have well and truly learnt by now that things rarely go as expected. I was making sure we had a backup plan.
A backup plan you chose not to share with us. Why? Who were you planning to turn into a vampyre?
You sound like Veliaf,. Clearly you've been spending too much time with him. It is not befitting of you.
I can do it your way if you prefer? I may be the last friend you have, Vanescula. If you want to have any chance of escaping this place, you should tell me what you were planning.
Should I? Tell me, do you know what this place is, ?
Does it matter?

It does to me. This was once the palace of the sycophant Lord Jovkai. When my brother first started to unite the vampyre clans, it was a long and slow process. Most resisted, the Jovkai in particular.
One battle against them was so devastating, that it risked undoing all that had been fought for to that point.
But don't forget, we were already starting to become civilised now, and so Lord Jovkai was invited to Castle Drakan for reparation discussions.
But when he arrived, he sat himself at the head of our table. He presented us with a banquet that he had brought himself.
And as he drank his wine, he told us that this was to be our reparations. We would be strangers in our own home, dining from his scraps.
When the meal was done, he decided it was my job to tidy up, so tidy I did. I took Lord Jovkai's cup and washed it in poison.
It was just a small amount of course. Not enough to kill him. But every night we dined, I did the same.
Over time, he grew more ill. He was tended to by the best, but it made no difference. Less than a year later, he was dead.
Why are you telling me this?
Because you seem to think this is me beaten, but you're mistaken. My brother would tell you that he alone united us, but were it not for me, we might still be dining at the behest of Lord Jovkai.

Now, as fun as all this has been, my brother will almost certainly be upon you and your new friends soon. Given you clearly don't need my help anymore, perhaps you should go and bother someone else instead.
Any luck with her?
I suspected as much. I wouldn't keep wasting time on her. We have more important things to worry about.
I suppose you're right.
What do you make of all this?

You mean Sugadinti? We just keep replacing one vampyre with another. Vanescula, her brother, and now him. Even if we do get back to Morytania, how long before we find ourselves having to deal with him as well?
It's not just him though.
Which makes it even worse. These aranei... Look at how they worship him! Imagine if the people of Morytania acted like that towards Drakan! Are we really allying ourselves with a cult now?
But what about Efaritay? Do you not think we can trust her at least?
It's been lifetimes since she was a queen. The things she's been through... we don't know what that did to her. Drakan's prisoner... now friends with a vampyre!
So you really don't trust her at all? Not even slightly?
We don't know her,.
No, but she might be the best hope we have now.
Hmm...
You still don't think we're getting out of this, do you?
There's a slim chance now, sure. But it's just that: slim. Besides, like I say, even if we do survive, what then?
Can you not imagine it? Sugadinti and Efaritay, leading Morytania side by side, with us there to help as well. This could be a real future!
No, I can't imagine it! And I don't need to imagine it, because it's never going to happen!
Like it or not, Veliaf, you need to face the facts! The reality is, you might actually survive this! And what then?! What happens when you finally accept that this isn't where it ends for you?!
A pub.
What?
That one in Burgh de Rott. Tidy it up, give it a new name. Maybe set up a brewery in the cellar...
That...
What would you serve?
Nothing fancy. Just good proper beers, brewed on site.
Some food surely?
Hmm... Maybe some nice pies? Would need someone else to cook them though.
Don't fancy yourself a chef?
Just probably best I don't kill all the patrons. Bad for business.
Very true...
What would you call it?
Myreque's Rest.
Well, I look forward to visiting it.
Hmph.
Best you go and get ready,. Won't be long until Drakan is here.
Welcome back, my child. I hope you are ready, for my disciples tell me that Drakan has been sighted. He is heading this way.
Ready as I'll ever be. What about the portal? How close are you to getting it made?
We are not far off, but more time is still needed. However, I have faith in my disciples. They will make sure that we have it.
And when we arrive in Morytania?
If all goes well, both of the Drakan siblings will be trapped here, and with both Efaritay and Safalaan out of their reach, they will have no way of escaping.
And what about all the vampyres left in Morytania?
Without a clear leader, chaos will ensue. That is... unless a new candidate steps in.
You?
Precisely... In time, I hope I can show you that I can offer both humans and vampyres something that neither Drakan can.
Once we are somewhere safer, I will explain everything. However, for now, we must focus on our survival.
What do you need me to do?
Nothing. As I say, my disciples have it in hand. They will buy us the time that we require. You need simply wait until the portal is ready.
They're going to fight Drakan? If that's the case, then I will join them.
That is very admirable of you, my child. However, it would be unwise of you to try and take on Drakan.
We need as much time as we can get. Even if I can make a small difference, it might be the difference between success and failure.
Very well. If that is your wish, I will not stop you, but if you are not back here by the time the portal opens, I'm afraid we will not be able to wait for you.
Don't worry about me. You just make sure that portal is ready.
I will see that it is. Now, my disciples are gathering on the bridge outside. You should collect some supplies from the kitchen if needed, then join them there. I wish you good luck, my child.
Lord Drakan is almost here, my friend. I pray to Father Sugadinti that you are adequately prepared.
? I did not expect to see you out here.
Is that you, Sarei? I'm here to help.
Your bravery is commendable, but you should not be here. Go back inside where it is safe.
If Drakan gets through, none of us will be safe. My place is here.
Very well, but be ready to fall back as soon as I tell you to.
You should go back upstairs, my friend. Once the portal is opened, there will likely not be much time to use it.
What about her?
You need not worry. We will ensure the prisoner does not get anywhere near that portal. Now go.
How much longer do we need?
As long as they can buy us.
They have no hope of standing against Drakan. Once he arrives, every last one of them will die.
They will. And they will do so willingly, because they know what will happen to us all if they don't.
It's no use!, fall back into the entrance hall!
I'm not leaving you out here!
Today is not the day you die, my friend! Go!
You shouldn't be here, Efaritay! You're too important!
If Drakan gets through those doors, it won't matter where I am! Now let's get this room secure!
The portal is ready, my lady! You must fall back!
Efaritay!
Let him go, Vanescula!
So you can leave me here to die? I don't think so! If you want him, you'll give me passage through that portal!
We don't have time for this, Efaritay!
I will not abandon my son! Let her through, Sugadinti!
Sugadinti... I see you survived. I also see that you have something of mine. Two things in fact.
I will be generous with you and allow you to keep one. The other you will return to me. Safalaan or Efaritay, the choice is yours.
You do not need Sugadinti to make a choice Drakan. I'm more than capable of making my own. If you want me, I'm right here!
Ivan! What happened?! Where is everyone else?
I think that spell must have done something to the portal. They could be anywhere!
And we're running out of time. Look at the sky...
It's starting to turn red!
Which can only mean one thing...
And that's not all. Look!
Already gathering their sacrifices for Drakan's festival!
What should we do?
We need to find the others. If Veliaf is with them, he'll have taken them somewhere safe.
Maybe the hideout in Meiyerditch?
Too risky surely? There's a lot of vampyres around there.
Burgh de Rott then?
Seems like the best option.
We'd better get over there then.
Ivan! ! Are you okay?
We're alright, Veliaf. It's good to see you in one piece.
What happened back there?
Drakan targeted the portal with some sort of spell. Doing so caused it to expand, sending us all here.
That means Drakan himself made it back. We failed.
We can't give up! There must still be a chance to stop him.
How? His blood moon is starting to rise. He'll already be preparing to start his festival, and given there's been no sign of Efaritay, I think it's pretty safe to say he has her.
Not to mention, all that's before we even consider Vanescula and Safalaan...
Sugadinti, you'd been preparing to overthrow Drakan for years. What was the original plan?
I'm afraid, my child, the original plan was cut short after your arrival in Vampyrium. However, given the situation we are in... I fear we will have to make do.
Meaning?
Our original hope was to gather allies here to support us in overthrowing Drakan. We had been preparing for this in multiple areas, though as I say, things were unfortunately cut short.
However, there is one individual here that we made good progress on recruiting. She is not yet aware of this, but I believe we have the means to ensure she... agrees to support us.
Who?
The being that is masquerading as my daughter.
The Nylocas Queen? So that's what we were preparing for in the Theatre. But I thought you were developing weapons to use against her?
We were, my child. It is my hope that I can offer her enough to join with us willingly. However, from what we've seen of her, it is clear she has rather lofty ambitions of her own.
I see. You need something to keep her in check.
Indeed... Now, time is of the essence. We must go to the Theatre at once.
What about Vanescula? She has Safalaan!
Veliaf's right. We can't just abandon him. Besides, the last thing we need when trying to deal with one Drakan is the other to be causing problems as well.
It is not my desire to abandon your friend. However, we have no idea where Vanescula might be or what she might be planning.
Well, we don't all need to go to the Theatre. Veliaf and I can find Vanescula while you two head over there.
Hmm... Very well. Some of my disciples will join you. They will send word to us as soon as you find out where she is.
No point wasting any time then. Let's go, Ivan.
The situation here in Hallowvale is... delicate, my child. To avoid attention, I would suggest we travel to Ver Sinhaza separately.
Do you think the Nylocas Queen's help will be enough?
In truth, my child, I'd have preferred we be in a situation where more allies were available to us. However, I still believe she will be enough for us to achieve victory.
Drakan is powerful, it is true. Indeed, he is one of the most powerful beings I have ever encountered. And yet, he is not immortal.
Even before considering the Nylocas Queen, we very much have the numbers on our side.
We had the numbers back in Vampyrium as well. All those aranei he killed...
Yes... My disciples fought bravely, but combat has always been a weakness for them. However, with the Nylocas Queen on our side, not only will we have the numbers, but the raw strength as well.
I hope you're right.
If we do defeat Drakan, what happens then?
We must ensure no power vacuum is left. As soon as he is dealt with, I must immediately step up as the new leader of the vampyres.
How do you know they'll accept you?
I'm sure some won't. However, most have no love for Drakan, and I plan to offer them something he couldn't.
That being?
A solution to their blood shortages. Their reliance on your kind must end. Luckily for us, in the short term, my disciples are more than willing to provide their blood.
And in the longer term?
There are many options open to us. Haemalchemy is likely to be the most promising.
But the humans of Morytania will finally be free? That's something you can promise?
It is. I give you my word.
And what about Vanescula? Where does she fit into this?
Once she is found, she will need dealing with as well.
How?
That is up to her. I am very much open to letting her live. Indeed, her experience with the vampyres here could be highly beneficial to ensuring a smooth transfer of power.
I doubt she'd help willingly.
I believe you to be correct, my child, and so if required, we must be ready to remove her from the picture more... permanently.
What do you think of this festival of Drakan's?
It is my personal view that the Vitur clan were already one of the more... civilised clans, even before the arrival of the Stranger from Afar.
The Drakan clan always disgusted us. Even by the standards back then, their ways were barbaric. Their Blood Moon festivals were the finest example of that.
They're barbaric even without the festivals. Just look at how they've treated humans here.

Yes, indeed... However, I can assure you, my child, that there is always another way. If you need an example of that, just look at my disciples. They are proof that vampyres can live side by side with other races.
Vanescula promised a future where humans and vampyres lived side by side as well.
I have no doubt that she did, but she is a Drakan as well, my child. Her ambition may well be greater than that of even her brother's. These lands would never see peace under her.
Do you think Efaritay will be okay?
I share your concern, my child, but I'm sure she will be fine. This is not the first time she has been Drakan's prisoner, and given he needs her blood for his festival, he has no reason to harm her.
The blood moon is already starting to rise though. We've already seen some vampyres capturing humans for the festival as well.
Yes... Time is not on our side, but as long as we can stop Drakan before the moon fully rises, his festival need not come to be.
Alright, I'll meet you there.
Welcome, my child. I must say... it is strange taking on a form like this. I never had much need of my shapeshifting abilities back in Vampyrium, but it seems wise to keep a low profile here.
The other vampyres will still be able to smell you.
They will, but most of them are not true vampyres. They are Drakan's creations. They will not know me, nor will they recognise my scent.
Besides, I think it's safe to say that given the impending festival, they'll have... more important matters to worry about.
I suppose the same can be said for us. What's the plan here?
As I said before, my hope is that I can convince this Nylocas Queen to willingly join with us. However, it is very possible she will resist... at least at first.
And you have a way to stop her if she does?
Yes... Thanks to your work, I was able to create a toxin that will be quite deadly to her and her children. I suspect it will help with persuading her... if required.
Are we going to have to fight through the Theatre to get to her?
I suspect not. If she has taken on my daughter's memories, she will be all too aware of who I am. She will not be able to resist an audience with me.
Makes sense. Shall we head in then?
Not quite. I actually have quite a specific task for you. While I have my audience with the Nylocas Queen, I would like you to ensure we are not... disturbed.
You will wait outside her chamber while I head in. If she resists, she will call her children to her, potentially along with some of her other pets. You must ensure they do not get to her.
Alright. I can do that.
Very good, my child. Let me know when you are ready to go in.
Here we are. Are you ready, my child?
I am. I'll make sure nothing gets in there.
Then let us begin, my child.
I'll be back shortly.
Do not take too long, my child.
Shall we head back inside, my child?
